text: The system shall refuse "not reportable" while an Unknown answer could make the event reportable.
Each market an event touches shall get its own assessment and its own signed conclusion.

text: An organisation rule shall not remove, reword or lower a floor question.
A later rule version shall never change a signed conclusion, which names the rule version it used.
The floor rules shall give the same outcome and report type as release 0.10.92 for every Yes/No/Unknown combination.
Each market shall use the reporting role, form and clock that match the organisation's role in that market.
For a country outside the five markets, an answer set with an Unknown shall never give "not reportable".
A deadline shall be the earlier of the deadlines counted in the authority's time zone and in the organisation's.
Every screen, export and reminder shall show the same deadline for the same market.
When no country is known, the shortest clock of every market shall apply.
The clock of a back-entered Case shall count from awareness, never from the entry time.
The daily deadline list shall be sent once per organisation per local day, also when nothing is due.
Awareness shall be the earliest known first knowledge, also after two records are linked.
A Case without an awareness date shall get a provisional clock and a clarification task.
An awareness later than the earliest known shall need a signature and, outside a trial, a second person.
A report of death, serious injury, a threat or a harm word shall put the Case on the fast track.

text: New information that raises the severity shall reopen triage with an alert.
A Case whose triage target is missed shall raise an overdue alert to the backup and the escalation role.
No path other than row 2 of the outcomes table, an override included, shall set "Service only".
A complaint shall not be down-graded to service.
A classification code shall never set a deadline, a trigger or a conclusion.
The routine path shall never close a complaint that needs a reportability assessment.
scenario_ids: RT-13 RT-14 RT-18 RT-19 RT-22 RT-24

text: A service record raised to a complaint shall keep its original awareness.
Every signing shall need the password session plus a fresh authenticator code.
Signature verification shall recompute the hash of the exact record version and snapshot the signature binds.
When two people sign the same record at once, the second signature shall be refused.
A signature shall be valid only when both the record and the signature are saved.
Only a user with signing authority and recorded signer training shall sign a regulated decision.
Outside a trial, the maker of a record shall not approve the same record.
An administrator shall never approve a regulated decision.
The rule register shall refuse a rule version whose approver is not a staff account allowed to approve rule content and different from the builder's staff account.
An audit row shall not be updated or deleted.
The audit hash chain shall be verified daily and on demand, reporting any break.
Every change to a regulated value shall be audited with the old value, the new value, the actor and the reason.
A change to a reporting fact, or a re-upload behind a signed decision, shall be refused without a reason.
A signed review of the audit trail, of access or of the configuration shall not change after signing.
A correction to a signed record shall supersede it, never edit it.
A submitted report shall never be overwritten.
An upgrade step shall never change the content of a signed record.
"Trace this value" shall show the field's real origin: its change, its import line and its snapshot.
A signed PMS document version shall never change after signing.
Records under legal hold, or before their retention date, shall not be purged.
3500A and eMDR values shall come only from the approved snapshot, never from a guess.
An authority report with a required block missing shall be refused by the report check before approval.
An EU or GB MIR XML file shall be served only from an approved, current snapshot.
No organisation shall read or change another organisation's data through any surface.
A background job shall run only in the scope of its event's organisation.
An imported row that fails a check shall go to quarantine with its reasons.
A repeated import of the same external identifier shall not create a second complaint.
An imported row that suggests harm shall reach triage, also when it is quarantined.
An e-mail accepted by the intake address shall become a draft Case stamped with the time the mail server received it.

text: Similar wording shall suggest possible duplicate pairs without merging records.
The sample clock shall move sample records only, never customer records.
The organisation export shall hold every record, file and the verified audit head, with a SHA-256 per entry.
An exported CSV cell that starts with a formula character shall be written as text.
An export download link shall be refused after its expiry and to any person other than the requester.
A backup shall restore into an empty database, with the audit chain verified and erasures re-applied.
A production backup older than 26 hours shall raise an alert.
A quarterly restore drill shall restore the latest backup, with its key, into an empty database.
After a restore, outbox events that occurred before the restore point shall be held and never sent again automatically.
A server clock offset over 1 second, or an unknown offset, shall be reported as not ok.
A notification that cannot be delivered shall be retried and, once dead-lettered, shown to operations.
MDARIX staff shall have no route that changes a customer organisation's regulated data.
A request from a deactivated account or with an expired session shall be refused.
An investigation conclusion shall not be submitted for review while a challenge question is unanswered.
A CAPA effectiveness check shall never read "effective" when the data are too few or too early.
A pattern to review shall be stated only above the set threshold, with its counts, units and rates.
Product 360 and Supplier 360 counts by product, version, lot and supplier shall equal the counts of the underlying records.
The Value Centre shall compute its medians from the organisation's own known data only.
